topic.title: Continual Learning, Retention, and Sequential Model Integration
topic.overview: Continual learning updates a system as tasks or data arrive while trying to preserve useful earlier knowledge. This cluster examines forgetting, backward transfer, replay, representation alignment, and sequential model merging. One representative study finds that intermediate features can forget less than final layers and uses auxiliary classifiers for both retention and earlier inference exits.
topic.whyItMatters: A deployed model may need repeated adaptation without access to its complete training history. Effective continual learning must balance new-task progress, historical performance, memory requirements, and inference cost rather than measuring only the latest task.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives include synaptic importance and generative replay. Later work analyzes which parameters forget and how new learning can benefit old tasks. Recent approaches extend the problem to in-context learning and merging adapted foundation models, including controllable paths through parameter space.
openQuestions: How should retention be valued when tasks differ in importance?
Can evaluation separate useful adaptation from performance preserved by storing increasing amounts of historical data?

papers.tldr: Pretraining interventions that favor flatter minima reduce reported forgetting after post-training and quantization, including in an existing billion-parameter checkpoint.

papers.title: Skill Neologisms: Towards Skill-based Continual Learning
papers.tldr: Learned vocabulary tokens improve specific skills and compose without joint training, suggesting a possible route to skill-based continual learning.

papers.title: Spectral Imbalance Causes Forgetting in Low-Rank Continual Adaptation
papers.tldr: Balancing the singular components of low-rank task updates reduces both disruption of past knowledge and vulnerability to later interference.

papers.title: Task-Driven Subspace Decomposition for Knowledge Sharing and Isolation in LoRA-based Continual Learning
papers.tldr: LoDA separates shared and task-specific LoRA directions to support knowledge transfer while controlling interference during continual learning.

papers.title: The Forgetting-Retention Dilemma: Certified Unlearning Theory in Continual Learning
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes unlearning in continual learning and develops a hybrid approach balancing targeted forgetting, retained performance, and storage cost.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Continual Factual Knowledge Acquisition of Language Models: From Theory to Algorithm
papers.tldr: A simplified theory of factual forgetting motivates STOC, which selects influential factual snippets to guide generative replay.

papers.title: Turning Back Without Forgetting: Selective Backward Refinement for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
papers.tldr: SABER selectively refines earlier task prompts using later knowledge, achieving positive backward transfer without replay in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Understanding Generalization and Forgetting in In-Context Continual Learning
papers.tldr: A theory of sequential tasks in a single prompt explains how shared attention can produce positive transfer, interference, and forgetting.

papers.title: Unlocking the Potential of Continual Model Merging: An ODE Perspective
papers.tldr: ODE-M turns continual model merging into a guided trajectory with a utility-aware stopping point to balance retained knowledge and incoming expertise.
